dense_er_scaling.description: Dense Erdos-Renyi polymatrix games (edge probability 0.12, 5 actions, N in {64,128,256,512}). Every submission runs at the same fixed privacy operating point (rounds, broadcast noise, per-round step allowance) on the same fixed games and noise; the score is exploitability of the empirical distribution of played profiles, relative to a fixed comparator calibrated to the same privacy budget and to uniform play.

comparator_exploitability_ratio.description: Mean over player counts of (summed CCE exploitability of the submission) / (summed CCE exploitability of the fixed structure-free private comparator at the same privacy budget). The paper's headline comparison. 10 = failed experiment.

relative_exploitability.description: Mean over instances of CCE exploitability divided by the exploitability of the uniform profile on the same game (1 = no better than uniform play, 0 = exact CCE). 10 = failed experiment.

relative_final_nash_gap.description: Mean over instances of the last-iterate Nash gap divided by the uniform profile's Nash gap. Secondary quality check of the final profile. 10 = failed experiment.

privacy_protocol_compliance.description: Fraction of required instances whose transcript passes the privacy-protocol checks (exact rounds, valid strategies, broadcasts = played strategy + fixed noise, bounded payoff-dependent movement). Any shortfall fails the experiment.

paper_reported.source: Figures 3 and 5 (dense Erdos-Renyi, A=5, p in {0.1,0.3,0.5}, N from 2^7 to 2^12), values read from the plots.
paper_reported.comparator_exploitability_ratio_note: 0.84 = mean over the plotted N of ours/baseline (about 0.92 at N=128 falling to about 0.75 at N=4096).

dense_er_scaling.scale_note: Scaled down: N in {64..512} instead of 2^7..2^12, one edge probability (0.12), the finite-scale operating point of data/polymatrix.benchmark_hyperparameters (T=8, eta=T^-1/3, sigma=T^-1/2) and a structure-free comparator instead of the paper's exact Huang et al. adaptation, whose constants are not given. Absolute exploitabilities are not comparable to the paper's (different utility scale); only the ratio is.

dense_cluster_scaling.description: Dense clustered polymatrix games (floor(1/p)=8 clusters, all intra-cluster pairs connected, cross-cluster probability 10p/N, 5 actions, N in {64,...,512}). Same fixed operating point, games, noise and comparator protocol as dense_er_scaling.

sparse_knn_scaling.description: Sparse geometric graphs: players at random points in the unit square, each connected to its 4 nearest neighbours (5 actions, N in {64,...,512}, T=2 or 3 rounds). Same fixed protocol; this is the regime where the paper's own method makes little exploitability progress.
